sections.crash_profile: From {{window_start}} to {{window_end}}, {{total_3y}} crashes occurred at this signalized four-leg intersection. There were {{ka_3y}} fatal or suspected serious injury crashes and {{kabc_3y}} KABCO injury crashes. Left-turn-opposing crashes were most frequent ({{left_turn_opposing_3y}}), followed by rear-end ({{rear_end_3y}}) and run-off-road ({{run_off_road_3y}}). Nighttime crashes were also notable ({{night_3y}}). Pedestrian and bicycle counts are not available.
sections.why_flagged: Flagged for high crash frequency and injury rate, with {{annual_fsi}} fatal or serious injuries per year and {{annual_kabc}} KABCO injuries per year. The intersection is ranked {{rank_city_actionable}} among actionable city sites, with risk factors including high traffic exposure ({{aadt}} vehicles/day), multiple marked crossings, and proximity to other crash sites.

countermeasures.rationale: Providing a left-turn lane on one major-road approach addresses the high frequency of left-turn-opposing crashes. The cited CMF {{cmf:267}} is a direct crash-type match for KABCO injury crashes, but requires engineering review for prerequisites and severity scope.

Modifying change plus clearance intervals to the studied ITE 1985 practice may help reduce overall crashes at signalized intersections. The cited CMF {{cmf:380}} covers all crash types and severities, but needs engineering review for area setting and severity scope.

sections.benefit_cost: A numerical benefit could not be computed for any candidate, as no audit-approved CMF, unit cost, or service life is available, and the severity scopes do not match fatal or serious injury crashes.
sections.next_steps: Review intersection geometry, traffic volumes, and existing equipment to confirm prerequisites for left-turn lane and signal timing modifications. Complete source verification and engineering review for both treatments. Consider site-specific constraints and coordinate with TxDOT as needed.
